title: The Air Canada CEO’s English-only condolences lost him his job—a warning for every global CEO | Fortune
summary: Air Canada CEO Michael Rousseau's decision to post a message of condolence in English after a fatal crash, instead of French, led to his retirement and sparked outrage in Quebec, a predominantly French-speaking region.
sentiment_reason: The incident caused a strong negative market impact due to the cultural insensitivity and violation of the Official Languages Act, overshadowing the intended message of sympathy and diverting attention from the company's resilience.
